title: Law to require licenses for package delivery warehouses
summary: This bill would require operators of last-mile delivery warehouses in New York City to get a two-year, $500 license from the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and to directly employ workers who sort and deliver packages, instead of using subcontractors. Operators would owe workers 30 days' notice before termination except for serious misconduct, must provide annual safety training, and could face penalties up to $1,000 per day for violations, with workers able to sue. The change would affect about 45,500 last-mile warehouse and delivery workers citywide and take effect 120 days after becoming law, with a longer phase-in for the direct-employment requirement.
